cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: arccosine of -0.5 in radians (2*pi/3)
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 2.094395102. Independently verified in Python: math.acos(-0.5) = 2.0943951023931957, which is exactly 2*pi/3 -> 2.094395102 at 9 dp

cases.description: The same example converted to degrees, as the documented Remark suggests
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 120. Independently verified: 2*pi/3 radians = 120 degrees exactly; the double-precision product is 120.00000000000001, which is 120 at 9 dp

cases.description: An argument above 1 is outside the documented domain
cases.expected_note: Excel documents that number "must be from -1 to 1"; an argument outside the domain of a real-valued math function is Excel's documented #NUM! case ("a formula or function contains invalid numeric values")

The sibling arccosine/arccotangent page for the same function family documents this explicitly ("If Number is a non-numeric value, ACOT returns the #VALUE! error value"); #VALUE! is Excel's documented error for an argument of the wrong type
